principles: Mirror the existing proven pattern (--git-common-dir at line 538) rather than inventing a new resolution scheme.
Keep main-repo behavior byte-identical; only change behavior for the broken from-worktree-cwd case.
Do not regress non-bootstrap callers: scope the change to a bootstrap-specific resolver, leave getRepoRoot untouched.
Prove the fix with a regression that is red on the old code and green on the new, wired into the validate battery.
drivers: Correctness: bootstrap must always land the new worktree under the main repo root.
Blast-radius minimization: getRepoRoot has a non-bootstrap caller (resolveWorktreePath) that wants show-toplevel-relative semantics.
Durability: a regression smoke prevents reintroduction.
Wrapper-root safety: the configured-gitRoot branch must still resolve the main root.

options.name: bootstrap-specific-resolver
pros: Zero blast radius on non-bootstrap callers (getRepoRoot untouched)
Byte-identical from main repo (common-dir parent == show-toplevel there)

options.name: mutate-getRepoRoot
cons: Changes semantics for resolveWorktreePath (non-bootstrap) which resolves stored worktree.path relative to repo root — could break existing-worktree resolution
Violates strict scope / byte-identical constraint for the non-bootstrap caller

rationale: Add a bootstrap-specific resolveMainRepoRoot helper using `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, called only from the resolveBootstrapGitRoot no-gitRoot path. This surgically fixes the bug while leaving getRepoRoot and its non-bootstrap caller resolveWorktreePath byte-identical. It mirrors the already-proven pattern at line 538 and keeps main-repo behavior unchanged (common-dir parent == show-toplevel from main). mutate-getRepoRoot is rejected: it would change semantics for the NON-bootstrap caller resolveWorktreePath, violating strict-scope and byte-identical constraints and raising regression risk.

preMortem.scenario: The fix breaks the wrapper-root configured-gitRoot path or a non-bootstrap getRepoRoot caller (resolveWorktreePath)
preMortem.trigger: Implementer changes getRepoRoot itself instead of adding a bootstrap-specific resolver, or alters the configured-gitRoot branch in resolveBootstrapGitRoot
preMortem.consequence: Existing-worktree resolution (resolveWorktreePath) or wrapper-root bootstrap regresses; worktrees resolve to the wrong root
preMortem.mitigation: Check ALL getRepoRoot callers (only resolveWorktreePath:452 + bootstrap:432) and leave the non-bootstrap one untouched; keep the configured-gitRoot branch (resolveStorySignedWorkspace) intact and unchanged; add a byte-identical-from-main assertion in the regression and verify the configured-gitRoot branch still yields the main root

preMortem.scenario: The --git-common-dir resolution returns a wrong/relative path on some platforms or repo layouts
preMortem.trigger: git returns a relative `.git` common dir and the code does not resolve it absolute against cwd, or the path does not end in `.git` (e.g. bare repo)
preMortem.consequence: Bootstrap joins worktreeDir under a malformed root; worktree created in the wrong place or bootstrap throws
preMortem.mitigation: Resolve the common dir absolute against cwd (mirror line 538: isAbsolute? else join(cwd, commonDir)); take dirname only when it ends in `.git`, else fall through to the existing getRepoRoot() fallback so behavior never gets worse than today; cover both from-worktree and from-main in the regression

preMortem.scenario: The regression smoke passes against BOTH old and new code (false green) so it never proves the fix
preMortem.trigger: The smoke does not set cwd to the existing worktree, or asserts only the from-main case, so the buggy nested path is never exercised
preMortem.consequence: The bug could regress later undetected; the validate battery gives false confidence
preMortem.mitigation: The smoke MUST run the bootstrap with cwd = the existing worktree directory and assert the new worktree is at <main>/.worktrees/B-new and NOT nested; explicitly verify red-on-old by temporarily reverting the resolver and confirming the smoke fails (transcript-diff.md captures nested-before / main-after)

preMortem.scenario: The regression smoke is added but never runs in the validate battery
preMortem.trigger: package.json wires a test:* script but does not chain it into the root `test` script or the lattice validate battery
preMortem.consequence: Smoke exists but provides no protection; reviewers/CI never run it
preMortem.mitigation: Wire the new test:* script into the chained root `test` and confirm root npm test actually executes it (grep the chained test string; run it and see it pass)
